## f

*n.* 1. **華氏度** — a degree on the Fahrenheit scale of temperature
2. **氟** — a nonmetallic univalent element belonging to the halogens; usually a yellow irritating toxic flammable gas; a powerful oxidizing agent; recovered from fluorite or cryolite or fluorapatite
3. **法拉** — the capacitance of a capacitor that has an equal and opposite charge of 1 coulomb on each plate and a voltage difference of 1 volt between the plates
4. the 6th letter of the Roman alphabet

## fable

**發音：** /ˈfeɪbəl/
*n.* 1. **寓言** — A fictitious narrative intended to enforce some useful truth or precept, usually with animals, etc. as characters; an apologue. Prototypically, Aesop's Fables.
2. **傳說, 寓言** — a story about mythical or supernatural beings or events
3. **神話 /神話, 傳說 /傳說** — Any story told to excite wonder; common talk; the theme of talk.
4. **謊言 /謊言** — Fiction; untruth; falsehood.
5. a deliberately false or improbable account
6. a short moral story (often with animal characters)
*v.* 1. *(archaic, intransitive)* **編造 /編造, 虛構 /虛構, 捏造** — To compose fables; hence, to write or speak fiction; to write or utter what is not true.
2. *(archaic, transitive)* **編造 /編造, 虛構 /虛構, 捏造** — To make up; to devise, and speak of, as true or real; to tell of falsely; to recount in the form of a fable.

## fabric

*“the fabric in the curtains was light and semitransparent”*
*“woven cloth originated in Mesopotamia around 5000 BC”*

3. the underlying structure
*“providing a factual framework for future research”*
*“it is part of the fabric of society”*

<a id="entry-f-000019"></a>
## fabric softener

**發音：** /ˈfæbrɪk ˈsɒfənər/
*n.* 1. *(countable, uncountable)* **織物柔軟劑 /織物柔軟劑, 柔順劑 /柔順劑** — A chemical agent used to prevent static cling and make fabric softer by coating the surface of the cloth fibers with a thin layer of chemicals; these chemicals have lubricant properties and are electrically conductive, thus making the fibers feel smoother and preventing buildup of static electricity; usually available as a liquid or as dryer sheets.

<a id="entry-f-000020"></a>
## fabricate

**發音：** /ˈfæb.ɹɪ.keɪt/
*v.* 1. **編造, 虛構, 偽造, 加工, 捏造** — make up something artificial or untrue
2. *(transitive)* **捏造, 偽造 /偽造, 編造 /編造** — To invent and form; to forge; to devise falsely.
3. *(transitive)* **製作 /製作, 製成 /製成** — To form into a whole by uniting its parts; to construct; to build.
4. **制, 生產, 加工, 製造** — put together out of artificial or natural components or parts
*“the company fabricates plastic chairs”*
*“They manufacture small toys; He manufactured a popular cereal"”*
5. *(transitive)* **製作 /製作, 製成 /製成** — To form by art and labor; to manufacture; to produce.
6. *(transitive)* **切碎, 屠宰** — To cut up an animal as preparation for cooking, particularly used in reference to fowl.

## fabrication

*n.* 1. **製造業, 加工, 製造** — the act of making something (a product) from raw materials

*“an improvement in the manufacture of explosives”*

3. a deliberately false or improbable account
4. writing in a fictional form
5. the deliberate act of deviating from the truth

## fabulous

**發音：** /ˈfæbjʊləs/

<a id="entry-f-000025"></a>
## face

**發音：** /ˈfeɪ̯s/
*n.* 1. **人類的臉, 臉, 顏, 面** — the front of the human head from the forehead to the chin and ear to ear
*“he washed his face”*
*“I wish I had seen the look on his face when he got the news”*
2. **表面** — the striking or working surface of an implement
3. **表面** — a surface forming part of the outside of an object
*“he examined all sides of the crystal”*
*“dew dripped from the face of the leaf”*
4. **表面** — the side upon which the use of a thing depends (usually the most prominent surface of an object)
*“he dealt the cards face down”*
5. **鬼臉** — a contorted facial expression
*“she made a grimace at the prospect”*
6. **厚顏無恥, 厚臉皮** — impudent aggressiveness
*“I couldn't believe her boldness”*
*“he had the effrontery to question my honesty”*
*v.* 1. **對抗** — oppose, as in hostility or a competition
*“You must confront your opponent”*
*“Jackson faced Smith in the boxing ring”*
2. **向, 朝, 面對, 面向, 面對著** — be oriented in a certain direction, often with respect to another reference point; be opposite to
*“The house looks north”*
*“My backyard look onto the pond”*
3. **對, 面對著, 面向, 面對** — be opposite
*“the facing page”*
*“the two sofas face each other”*
4. *(transitive)* **朝, 對 /對** — To position oneself or itself so as to have one's face closest to (something).
5. *(transitive)* **面臨 /面臨** — To deal with (a difficult situation or person); to accept (facts, reality, etc.) even when undesirable.
6. deal with (something unpleasant) head on
*“You must confront your problems”*
*“He faced the terrible consequences of his mistakes”*

<a id="entry-f-000070"></a>
## facility

**發音：** /fəˈsɪlɪti/
*n.* 1. **設施, 設備** — a building or place that provides a particular service or is used for a particular industry
*“the assembly plant is an enormous facility”*
2. *(countable, uncountable)* **設備 /設備** — The physical means or contrivances to make something (especially a public service) possible; the required equipment, infrastructure, location etc.
3. **靈巧, 熟練** — skillful performance or ability without difficulty
*“his quick adeptness was a product of good design”*
*“he was famous for his facility as an archer”*
4. a natural effortlessness
*“they conversed with great facility”*
*“a happy readiness of conversation"--Jane Austen”*

## familial

**發音：** /fəˈmɪljəl/
*adj.* 1. *(not-comparable)* **家庭的** — Of or pertaining to a human family.

*“children of the same familial background”*
*“familial aggregation”*
3. **遺傳+的** — occurring among members of a family usually by heredity

<a id="entry-f-000307"></a>
## familiar

**發音：** /fəˈmɪl.i.ə/
*adj.* 1. **常見+的, 熟悉+的** — well known or easily recognized
*“a familiar figure”*
*“familiar songs”*
2. **熟悉** — Known to one, or generally known; commonplace.
3. **熟悉** — Acquainted.
4. **熟悉** — Intimate or friendly.
5. within normal everyday experience; common and ordinary; not strange
*“familiar ordinary objects found in every home”*
*“a familiar everyday scene”*
6. (usually followed by `with') well informed about or knowing thoroughly
*“conversant with business trends”*
*“familiar with the complex machinery”*
*n.* 1. **使魔** — An attendant spirit, often in animal or demon form.
2. a person attached to the household of a high official (as a pope or bishop) who renders service in return for support
3. a friend who is frequently in the company of another
*“drinking companions”*
*“comrades in arms”*
4. a spirit (usually in animal form) that acts as an assistant to a witch or wizard

<a id="entry-f-000308"></a>

2. usualness by virtue of being familiar or well known

*“We familiarized ourselves with the new surroundings”*

<a id="entry-f-000313"></a>
## family

*n.* 1. **人家, 家庭成員, 家族, 家庭, 戶** — a social unit living together
*“he moved his family to Virginia”*
*“It was a good Christian household”*
2. **親屬, 親戚, 氏族, 民族, 家屬** — people descended from a common ancestor
*“his family has lived in Massachusetts since the Mayflower”*
3. primary social group; parents and children
*“he wanted to have a good job before starting a family”*
4. a collection of things sharing a common attribute
*“there are two classes of detergents”*
5. a person having kinship with another or others
*“he's kin”*
*“he's family”*
6. (biology) a taxonomic group containing one or more genera
*“sharks belong to the fish family”*

2. *(broadly, uncountable)* **風水 /風水** — An ancient Chinese system of geomancy used to design buildings and graves, and to determine the spatial arrangement of things, according to rules about the flow of energy, aimed at achieving harmony with the environment, promoting good fortune and wealth, etc.

## Fermat's Last Theorem

*prop. n.* 1. **費馬大定理 /費馬大定理** — The theorem that the Diophantine equation aⁿ+bⁿ=cⁿ has no solutions for positive integers a,b,c,n, where n>2.

<a id="entry-f-001582"></a>
## Fermat's principle

*prop. n.* 1. **費馬原理 /費馬原理** — The principle, which links geometrical optics (or "ray optics") with wave optics, that the path traversed by a ray between two given points is: (in the original "strong" formulation) the one that takes the least time, or (in a weaker but more general formulation) one that takes a time that is "stationary" with respect to variations of the path (so that, loosely speaking, a small change in the ray path entails a very small change in the traversal time).

<a id="entry-f-001584"></a>
## ferment

**發音：** /fəˈmɛnt/
*n.* 1. **紛亂, 騷動, 動亂** — a state of agitation or turbulent change or development
*“the political ferment produced new leadership”*
*“social unrest”*
2. **酵素, 酶** — a substance capable of bringing about fermentation
3. **發酵, 發酵作用** — a process in which an agent causes an organic substance to break down into simpler substances; especially, the anaerobic breakdown of sugar into alcohol
*v.* 1. **發酵 /發酵** — To react, using fermentation; especially to produce alcohol by aging or by allowing yeast to act on sugars; to brew.
2. be in an agitated or excited state
*“The Middle East is fermenting”*
*“Her mind ferments”*
3. work up into agitation or excitement
*“Islam is fermenting Africa”*
4. cause to undergo fermentation
*“We ferment the grapes for a very long time to achieve high alcohol content”*
*“The vintner worked the wine in big oak vats”*
5. go sour or spoil
*“The milk has soured”*
*“The wine worked”*

## fire

*v.* 1. **排放, 釋放, 發射, 解僱** — cause to go off
*“fire a gun”*
*“fire a bullet”*
2. **開除, 解僱, 遣散** — terminate the employment of; discharge from an office or position
*“The boss fired his secretary today”*
*“The company terminated 25% of its workers”*
3. **驅散, 驅逐** — drive out or away by or as if by fire
*“The soldiers were fired”*
*“Surrender fires the cold skepticism”*
4. **使出現, 喚起, 引起** — call forth (emotions, feelings, and responses)
*“arouse pity”*
*“raise a smile”*
5. **燒光, 燒燬** — destroy by fire
*“They burned the house and his diaries”*
6. start firing a weapon
*n.* 1. **火焰, 火舌, 焚燒, 火, 燃燒** — the process of combustion of inflammable materials producing heat and light and (often) smoke
*“fire was one of our ancestors' first discoveries”*
2. **灶火, 爐火** — a fireplace in which a relatively small fire is burning
*“they sat by the fire and talked”*
3. **火, 火元素** — once thought to be one of four elements composing the universe (Empedocles)
4. **熱心, 熱情** — feelings of great warmth and intensity
*“he spoke with great ardor”*
5. **抨擊, 譴責** — intense adverse criticism
*“Clinton directed his fire at the Republican Party”*
*“the government has come under attack”*
6. the event of something burning (often destructive)
*“they lost everything in the fire”*

## fit

**發音：** /fɪt/
*v.* 1. **適應, 適合, 符合** — be agreeable or acceptable to
*“This suits my needs”*
2. **適合, 合適, 符合** — be the right size or shape; fit correctly or as desired
*“This piece won't fit into the puzzle”*
3. **合適, 適宜, 配合, 符合** — satisfy a condition or restriction
*“Does this paper meet the requirements for the degree?”*
4. **匹配, 配合, 對應, 符合, 一致** — be compatible, similar or consistent; coincide in their characteristics
*“The two stories don't agree in many details”*
*“The handwriting checks with the signature on the check”*
5. **合身, 合適, 適合** — conform to some shape or size
*“How does this shirt fit?”*
6. **供應, 準備, 配備** — provide with (something) usually for a specific purpose
*“The expedition was equipped with proper clothing, food, and other necessities”*
*n.* 1. **發脾氣, 歇斯底里** — a display of bad temper
*“he had a fit”*
*“she threw a tantrum”*
2. **發作, 痙攣** — a sudden uncontrollable attack
*“a paroxysm of giggling”*
*“a fit of coughing”*
3. the manner in which something fits
*“I admired the fit of her coat”*
4. a sudden flurry of activity (often for no obvious reason)
*“a burst of applause”*
*“a fit of housecleaning”*
*adj.* 1. **健全+的, 健康+的** — physically and mentally sound or healthy
*“felt relaxed and fit after their holiday”*
*“keeps fit with diet and exercise”*
2. **合適 /合適** — Suitable; proper
3. meeting adequate standards for a purpose
*“a fit subject for discussion”*
*“it is fit and proper that you be there”*
4. (usually followed by `to' or `for') on the point of or strongly disposed
*“in no fit state to continue”*
*“fit to drop”*

## fix

**發音：** /ˈfɪks/
*v.* 1. **修理, 修補, 修復** — restore by replacing a part or putting together what is torn or broken
*“She repaired her TV set”*
*“Repair my shoes please”*
2. **固定, 使固定** — cause to be firmly attached
*“fasten the lock onto the door”*
*“she fixed her gaze on the man”*
3. **做菜, 烹調, 煮, 做** — prepare for eating by applying heat
*“Cook me dinner, please”*
*“can you make me an omelette?”*
4. **修理, 校準, 固定, 安裝** — kill, preserve, and harden (tissue) in order to prepare for microscopic study
5. *(obsolete, transitive)* **修理, 固定, 安裝 /安裝** — To pierce; now generally replaced by transfix.
6. **使準備好, 使適合, 準備, 裝備, 起草** — make ready or suitable or equip in advance for a particular purpose or for some use, event, etc
*“Get the children ready for school!”*
*“prepare for war”*
*n.* 1. **處於劣勢, 逆境, 困境** — informal terms for a difficult situation
*“he got into a terrible fix”*
*“he made a muddle of his marriage”*
2. something craved, especially an intravenous injection of a narcotic drug
*“she needed a fix of chocolate”*
3. the act of putting something in working order again
4. an exemption granted after influence (e.g., money) is brought to bear
*“collusion resulted in tax fixes for gamblers”*
5. a determination of the place where something is
*“he got a good fix on the target”*

## focal length

*n.* 1. **焦距** — A measure of how strongly an optical system converges or diverges light, the inverse of optical power. In the simple case of a single convex lens, it is the distance along the optical axis from the principal plane of the lens to the lens's focal point (where, for instance, the film would be placed in a camera). For more complex or multi-element optical systems, focal length need not correspond to any obvious measurable physical distance.
2. the distance from a lens to its focus

<a id="entry-f-003258"></a>
## force

**發音：** /fɔːs/
*v.* 1. **要挾, 迫, 逼, 逼迫, 強制** — to cause to do through pressure or necessity, by physical, moral or intellectual means :"She forced him to take a job in the city"
*“He squeezed her for information”*
2. **推, 推動** — move with force, "He pushed the table into a corner"
3. **拖, 拖拉, 拉** — cause to move by pulling
*“draw a wagon”*
*“pull a sled”*
4. **強迫 /強迫, 迫使, 迫, 逼迫, 逼, 脅迫 /脅迫** — To compel (an adversary or partner) to trump a trick by leading a suit that he/she does not hold.
5. urge or force (a person) to an action; constrain or motivate
6. impose urgently, importunately, or inexorably
*“She forced her diet fads on him”*
*n.* 1. **力氣, 力量, 勢力** — physical energy or intensity
*“he hit with all the force he could muster”*
*“it was destroyed by the strength of the gale”*
2. **軍事力量** — a unit that is part of some military service
*“he sent Caesar a force of six thousand men”*
3. **暴力** — an act of aggression (as one against a person who resists)
*“he may accomplish by craft in the long run what he cannot do by force and violence in the short one”*
4. **力量, 影響力, 勢力** — one possessing or exercising power or influence or authority
*“the mysterious presence of an evil power”*
*“may the force be with you”*
5. *(countable)* **武力** — Anything that is able to make a substantial change in a person or thing.
6. a powerful effect or influence
*“the force of his eloquence easily persuaded them”*

## free

**發音：** /fɹiː/
*adj.* 1. **自由+的, 解放+的** — able to act at will; not hampered; not under compulsion or restraint
*“free enterprise”*
*“a free port”*
2. **贈送+的, 免費+的** — costing nothing
*“complimentary tickets”*
*“free admission”*
3. **空+的, 空閒+的** — not occupied or in use
*“a free locker”*
*“a free lane”*
4. **自由的** — Not imprisoned or enslaved.
5. **自由的, 空閒 /空閑 /空閒** — Without obligations.
6. **自由的** — With no or only freedom-preserving limitations on distribution or modification.
*v.* 1. **使自由, 解放, 豁免, 釋放** — grant freedom to; free from confinement
2. **除掉, 幹掉, 消滅, 擺脫** — relieve from
*“Rid the house of pests”*
3. **使免除, 使自由** — grant relief or an exemption from a rule or requirement to
*“She exempted me from the exam”*
4. **解僱, 釋放** — free from obligations or duties
5. **免除, 赦免** — let off the hook
*“I absolve you from this responsibility”*
6. *(transitive)* **解放** — To make free; set at liberty; release.
*n.* 1. people who are free
*“the home of the free and the brave”*
*adv.* 1. **不受約束+地, 松+地, 鬆弛+地, 鬆散+地, 自由+地** — without restraint
*“cows in India are running loose”*

## function

**發音：** /ˈfʌŋ(k)ʃən/
*n.* 1. **映射, 函數** — (mathematics) a mathematical relation such that each element of a given set (the domain of the function) is associated with an element of another set (the range of the function)
2. **作用, 機能, 功能** — what something is used for
*“the function of an auger is to bore holes”*
*“ballet is beautiful but what use is it?”*
3. **功能, 機能 /機能** — What something does or is used for.
4. **功能** — The physiological activity of an organ or body part.
5. **職務 /職務, 職位 /職位** — A professional or official position.
6. **函數** — a relation such that one thing is dependent on another
*“height is a function of age”*
*“price is a function of supply and demand”*
*v.* 1. *(intransitive)* **工作, 運行 /運行, 運轉 /運轉** — To carry out a function; to be in action.
2. perform as expected when applied
*“The washing machine won't go unless it's plugged in”*
*“Does this old car still run well?”*
3. serve a purpose, role, or function
*“The tree stump serves as a table”*
*“The female students served as a control group”*
4. perform duties attached to a particular office or place or function
*“His wife officiated as his private secretary”*

<a id="entry-f-004310"></a>

<a id="entry-f-004311"></a>
## functional

**發音：** /ˈfʌŋkt͡ʃənəl/
*adj.* 1. **有作用+的, 功能+的** — designed for or capable of a particular function or use
*“a style of writing in which every word is functional”*

*“the problem now is not a constitutional one; it is a functional one"”*

4. **可使用的, 可操作的, 合用+的, 能用+的, 起作用的** — fit or ready for use or service
*“the toaster was still functional even after being dropped”*
*“the lawnmower is a bit rusty but still usable”*
5. involving or affecting function rather than physiology
*“functional deafness”*
6. designed for or adapted to a function or use
*“functional education selects knowledge that is concrete and usable rather than abstract and theoretical”*
*“functional architecture”*

## futurism

**發音：** /ˈfjuːt͡ʃəɹɪzəm/
*n.* 1. *(countable, uncountable)* **未來主義 /未來主義** — An early 20th century avant-garde art movement focused on speed, the mechanical, and the modern, which took a deeply antagonistic attitude to traditional artistic conventions.
2. an artistic movement in Italy around 1910 that tried to express the energy and values of the machine age
3. the position that the meaning of life should be sought in the future

<a id="entry-f-004483"></a>
## futurist

*n.* 1. a theologian who believes that the Scripture prophecies of the Apocalypse (the Book of Revelation) will be fulfilled in the future
2. someone who predicts the future
*adj.* 1. **未來派的** — In the style of futurism.
2. **未來主義+的** — of or relating to futurism
*“futurist art”*

<a id="entry-f-004484"></a>
## futuristic

*adj.* 1. **未來主義+的** — of or relating to futurism
*“futurist art”*

<a id="entry-f-004485"></a>
## futurity

*n.* 1. **今後, 以後, 未來, 將來** — the time yet to come
2. the quality of being in or of the future

<a id="entry-f-004486"></a>
## futurology

*n.* 1. *(uncountable, usually)* **未來學 /未來學** — The scientific forecasting of future trends in science, technology or society
2. the study or prediction of future developments on the basis of existing conditions

## Fuzhou

**發音：** /ˈfuˈt͡ʃoʊ/
*prop. n.* 1. **福州** — A prefecture-level city, the provincial capital of Fujian, China.
2. **撫州 /撫州** — A prefecture-level city in northeastern Jiangxi, China.

<a id="entry-f-004497"></a>
## fuzz

*n.* 1. **絨毛** — filamentous hairlike growth on a plant
*“peach fuzz”*
2. **條子** — uncomplimentary terms for a policeman
3. a hazy or indistinct representation
*“it happened so fast it was just a blur”*
*“he tried to clear his head of the whisky fuzz”*
4. the first beard of an adolescent boy

<a id="entry-f-004498"></a>
## fuzzy

*adj.* 1. **模糊不清的, 不清晰的, 不清楚的, 朦朧+的, 模糊+的** — indistinct or hazy in outline
*“a landscape of blurred outlines”*
*“the trees were just blurry shapes”*
2. covering with fine light hairs
*“his head fuzzed like a dandelion gone to seed”*
3. confused and not coherent; not clearly thought out
*“a vague and fuzzy idea of the world of finance”*

<a id="entry-f-004499"></a>
## fuzzy logic

*n.* 1. *(countable, uncountable)* **弗晰邏輯 /弗晰邏輯, 模糊邏輯 /模糊邏輯** — A form of reasoning, derived from fuzzy set theory, whereby a truth value need not be exactly zero (false) or one (true), but rather can be zero, one, or any value in between.
2. a form of mathematical logic in which truth can assume a continuum of values between 0 and 1

<a id="entry-f-004500"></a>
## fyke

*n.* 1. **長袋網** — A type of fish-trap consisting of tubular nets that are supported by hoops.

<a id="entry-f-004501"></a>
## fynbos

*n.* 1. *(uncountable)* **凡波斯** — Vegetation unique to the Cape Floral Kingdom, largely scrub, exceptionally biodiverse, including particularly large numbers of species of Proteaceae, Restionaceae, and Ericaceae.

<a id="entry-f-004502"></a>
## FYP

*n.* 1. *(abbreviation, alt-of, initialism)* **推薦頁 /推薦頁, 主頁 /主頁, 首頁 /首頁** — Initialism of for you page (“a user's home page on TikTok which consists of content automatically selected for that user”).

<a id="entry-f-004503"></a>
## Führer

**發音：** /ˈf(j)ʊə.ɹə/
*n.* 1. *(Nazism, definite, historical)* **元首** — Adolf Hitler, during his time as chancellor of Nazi Germany.
2. *(broadly)* **head of state) 元首, 領袖 /領袖, 領袖, 富勒爾 /富勒爾** — A leader, especially one exercising tyrannical power.
